_doc: Hand-kept assumptions and published figures for the 'what is a found bug worth' charts (value_v4.py) and BUG-VALUE.md. Every value names its source and how solid it is; change one and re-render to see the charts, titles and report move. Money in US dollars.

engineer_usd_per_hour.source: US BLS: software developers' median pay $135,980 a year (May 2025, Occupational Outlook Handbook); employer costs about 1.28x that net of paid leave (BLS Employer Costs for Employee Compensation, Sep 2026); about 1,830 hours actually worked a year. About $95 per hour worked.

reading_words_per_minute.source: below the 238 words a minute average for silent reading of non-fiction (Brysbaert 2019, Journal of Memory and Language, a meta-analysis), because review comments quote code

triage_seconds_per_comment.source: an assumption, on top of reading: about 50 s in all for an average QuickReview comment. The one measurement we found is shorter: reviewers took a median 16-28 s to evaluate an LLM review comment, reading included (Olewicki et al. 2024, a preprint), so this overstates QuickReview's reading cost

fix_hours.source: NIST Planning Report 02-3 (2002): hours to fix a bug found in coding or unit test against one found after release. Weak evidence: a 2002 survey of a handful of developers, effort only, no outage or customer cost

escape_share.label: 1 in 10
escape_share.source: a scenario, not a measurement: one missed serious defect in ten reaches production and costs the extra post-release hours; the other nine cost nothing more. Nobody has measured this share for code review.

ladder.title_fmt: One more catch: {catch}. Fixing after release: {release}
ladder.source_line:
Fix hours: NIST Planning Report 02-3 (2002), a small survey, effort only. Outage: Uptime Institute Annual Outage Analysis 2025, operators' own estimates.
Breach: IBM/Ponemon Cost of a Data Breach 2025, all causes, few of them code. Engineer time at $95 an hour (BLS). Ours: AACR-Bench, see value-price.

rungs.label: Fix a bug found in coding
Fix a bug found after release
